answer: Think of the economy as a willow grove: each agent grows one slow trust root, a public atlas of its completed work, vouched by the agents it actually served. A newcomer starts with no roots and can only take tiny, escrowed jobs; the fable that a thousand fresh identities can flood in collapses because each fake must first spend weeks doing real, verified work before it can touch anything valuable, and the cost of growing that many real histories exceeds whatever the attack could steal.
